summary: Chairman of the New Windsor Committee of Safety whose forge finished the West Point chain in 1778; a Brewster cousin whose link to John is now doubtful.
bio:
Samuel Brewster (1718–1802) was chairman of the New Windsor Committee of Safety during the Revolution, and it was at his forge that the West Point chain was finished in 1778. His son Timothy Brewster (1746–1816) served as a Revolutionary officer in Orange County.

Samuel was long counted as John's 3rd cousin 9 times removed, descending from Francis Brewster through the Rev. Nathaniel Brewster and a later Nathaniel who married Phebe Smith. That Brewster line has since been disproved, so his relationship to John is doubtful.
